key_insight: Bulky ligand substituents suppress intermolecular magnetic interactions in a five-Cu(II) metallacrown, revealing competing antiferromagnetic couplings and an S = 1/2 ground state.
engineering_relevance: Ligand-based magnetic isolation provides a route to studying intrinsic exchange interactions in molecular spin systems.
method: Modify salicylhydroxamate ligands with sterically bulky substituents.
Probe spin states using static magnetization and X-band/high-frequency EPR.
Compare exchange couplings and g-factors with broken-symmetry DFT.
evidence_signal: Magnetization yields J₁ = −8.1(2) THz, J₂ = −4.40(12) THz, and a doublet-to-quartet gap of 4.8(4) THz; EPR resolves near-axial g-factors of 2.028, 2.056, and 2.222.
watch_item: The abstract establishes molecular magnetic properties but does not demonstrate device integration or operational spin coherence.
paper_title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
